hypotheses.rationale: Couriers_online falls from 49 to 17 in the 240-min window and couriers_idle ~0 then; many orders open at 240 and high bad rates—points to lack of available couriers.
Dispatch queue mean spikes to 15.4 (max 30) at 240, indicating dispatch service becoming slow and queueing, causing assignment delays and open orders.

args.rationale: Add couriers should immediately reduce bad orders if courier_scarcity; increasing dispatcher workers should reduce bad orders if dispatcher_saturation. If dispatch calls are hanging, increasing workers will not improve (they'll block) while adding couriers won't help.

args.summary: Evidence shows a sharp drop in couriers_online (q3) and near-zero couriers_idle (q4) at the time the bad-order rate rose. Dispatch queue also grew (q2) but the pattern (many restaurants with open orders in q1) and the large improvement when adding couriers (part of x5) indicate lack of available couriers caused assignment delays and late/open orders. Recommend bringing ~20 couriers online immediately; monitor idle and queue metrics.

args.summary: Low idle-courier availability coincided with a high dispatch queue. Adding 10 couriers materially reduced bad-order rate by 0.238 (95% CI -0.262 to -0.214) and click-to-door time, while increasing dispatcher workers produced only a smaller improvement (-0.071). This supports courier scarcity as the primary cause; dispatcher load may be secondary.
